Facts in short are that Petitioner as plaintiff filed Title suit No. 171 of 1981 in the court of the subordinate judge, Chandpur stating that the suit land measuring an area of 3.81 acres of Khatian No. 421 of Mouza Chandpur originally belonged to C. S. recorded tenant Nadia Basi Das and Nagar Basi Das in 3/4th and 1/4th share respectively and that Nadia Basi Das transferred his Atli interest to Gasai Das by registered kabalas and that Nadia Basi Das died leaving 4 sons panchkori Das. Rajani Das, Aswirii Das, Bogola Kanta Das and that panchkori Das died leaving daughter in law Sree Moti who died leaving 2 sons .Dinesh and Umesh (Defendant„.No. 2 and 3) respectively who inherited 4 annas share of Nadia Basi Das in the jote and Aswani Das died leaving 2 full brothers Rajani and Bogia and a widow who subsequently died leaving the above named husband's brothers and that Bogla kanta Das died leaving full brother Rajani and a widow who died issueless.

Mr. Faruq also submits that compensation of 10% is to low keeping in view the long period of gap covering the period transaction held in 1975 the date of judgment pronounced in the year of 1987 and within this space of 12 years prices of goods and services including of lands definitely did not increase to so low rate of 10% Mr. Faruq lastly submits that the land in question in khatian 421 measuring 3.81 acres and the dispute is only with respect to an area of 561/2 decimels and this area comprises of homestead and the petitioners could have been given. 561/2 acres of land out of the remainder 3.81 acres of land 3.81 — 56 1/2 = 3.241/2 

 13. Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned counsel at the very outset of his submission took me through the definition of the Hindu undivided joint family, 'House' which has been elaborately discussed in the case of khirode Chandra Ghose and another Vs. Sarode prased Moitra reported in G. L. J. (1910) V 10.. XII page 525. The it has been bald that the term house embraces not merely the structure or building but includes also adjacent building curtilage. Gardens courtyard orchard and all that in necessary for the convenient use and occupation of the house but not that which is only for the personal use and convenience of the occupier. It includes the land of which the structured of the dwelling house stands. The test to be applied in what is necessary for the convenient use and occupation of the house. Mr. Dutta referring to the above decision also took me through relevant portion of the portion of judgment of the Appellate Court where it appears that there has been substantial consideration of all the relevant points of question that were required to be determined in the suit or appeal. So, Mr. Dutta, submits that R. S. khatian No. 421 measuring 3.81 acres comprised and accompanies the undivided Hindu dwelling house. The principle that the Appellate Court whether reversing or affirming the decision of the trial court, must arrive at its own independent finding on the issues involved in the case has been fully and adequately observed and complied with. Mr. Dutta further submits that according to definition of undivided' joint family house as given in the decision of 12 C. L. J. quoted above entire land in khatian 'No. 421 measuring 3.81 acres comes within the definition of House to such submission of the learned Advocate of the petitioner to the effect that the petitioner in the remained of 3.81 of land has got no substance and cannot be accepted.
